title: Prizzi's Honor
tagline: Love, honour and a very complicated wedding.
about: A Brooklyn mob hitman falls for a woman who turns out to be in the same line of work.
cue: Serve dessert at the wedding, when Charley first spots Irene.
faces: Supper in honour of Don Corrado's granddaughter
A Brooklyn church. The whole Prizzi family turns up.
Saffron rice round a mozzarella heart, fried gold, marinara.
Light crisp batter, sea salt and a squeeze of lemon.
First dance. He never got her name.
Escarole and tiny veal meatballs in clear chicken brodo.
Slow sausage sugo, ricotta and mozzarella, baked until blistered.
The old man's favourite. Seconds are not optional.
Pounded thin, seared fast, white wine, lemon, capers and butter.
Shaved fine, sharp and cold. Quick, and very clean.
Crackled almond cookies in icing sugar, tied in tulle.
The Don, Sunday coffee in the garden.
Sugared, five to a bag: health, wealth, happiness, children, long life.
THE DON TAKES FIRST PICK. WAIT.
Eat. Enjoy. Nobody leaves before the cake. Nobody.
With the compliments of the family. Envelopes to Angelo at the door.
Printed for the reception, 720 Court Street, Brooklyn, 1985.

    StartersThe bride's antipastoLemon-marinated mushrooms, salami, olives, artichokes.To begin, at the Prizzi wedding.How to make it200g button mushrooms2 tbsp olive oil1/2 lemon, juiced1 garlic clove, crushed1 tbsp chopped parsley100g salami, sliced120g mixed olives150g marinated artichokes, drainedBlanch the mushrooms in boiling water for 1 minute and drain well.Toss with olive oil, lemon juice, garlic and parsley. Refrigerate covered overnight.Serve on a platter with the salami, olives and artichokes.Zucchini frittiLight crisp batter, sea salt and a squeeze of lemon.Antipasti for the family.How to make it2 zucchinis, about 400g130g plain flour, divided150ml cold sparkling water500ml neutral oil, for frying1/4 tsp salt1/2 lemon, cut in wedgesCut the zucchini into batons, pat dry and toss with 30g of the flour.Whisk the remaining flour with the sparkling water into a light batter.Heat the oil to 185°C and fry the battered batons in small batches for 3 minutes until crisp and golden.Drain, season with salt and serve with lemon.MainsDon Corrado's baked zitiSlow sausage sugo, ricotta and mozzarella, baked until blistered.The old man's favourite. Seconds are not optional.How to make it400g Italian sausages1 tbsp olive oil1 onion, diced2 garlic cloves, crushed700g passata150ml water1 tsp dried oregano350g ziti or penne250g ricotta1/2 tsp salt and pepper, mixed200g mozzarellaRemove the sausages from their casings and brown in the oil, breaking up the meat.Add the onion for 5 minutes, then the garlic for 1 minute.Add the passata, water and oregano and simmer gently, stirring.Boil the ziti for 2 minutes less than the packet time and drain. Mix the ricotta with the seasoning.Layer pasta, sugo, ricotta and mozzarella in an ovenproof dish.Bake at 200°C for 25 minutes until blistered and rest for 10 minutes.SweetsWedding amarettiCrackled almond cookies in icing sugar, tied in tulle.Ice or cake? This is the cake.How to make it2 egg whites250g almond meal200g caster sugar1/2 tsp almond extract40g icing sugarWhisk the egg whites to stiff peaks in a clean bowl.Gently fold in the almond meal, caster sugar and almond extract.Shape into 20 small balls, roll in icing sugar and space on lined trays.Bake at 170°C for 15 minutes until crackled and lightly golden.Cool on the trays for 10 minutes, then move to a rack.DrinksWhite peach BelliniWhite peach purée topped with cold prosecco.The toast, the night Charley spots the lady in lavender.How to make it2 ripe white peaches2 tsp lemon juice1 tsp caster sugar480ml prosecco, chilledPeel and stone the peaches, blend with the lemon juice and sugar until smooth.Chill the purée for 30 minutes.Spoon some purée into each chilled flute and top slowly with prosecco poured down the side. Stir once and serve straight away.
